capabilities.description: Load and validate track YAML files at startup against the shipped track.v1.schema.json (draft 2020-12, additionalProperties false, required header fields, rubric with 5 x 20-point criteria, weights summing to 100, length_weeks minimum 4). An invalid file is refused with the offending field path name

Enrol a learner on a track with start_date and timezone, generate the 16-week x 6-session calendar from the fixed session template (day offsets 0,1,2,4,5,6 with framework/case_prep/case_class/lab/lab/exam durations), store the enrolment with its pinned track version, and send the week-1 reading emai

Run a chat session per scheduled session in six kernel modes (lecture, brief, socratic, sparring, oral_quiz, examiner), storing the transcript and writing an audit row per session; faculty content is built only from the week's track data, and sparring mode refuses to write the learner's deliverable.

A separate grader with no access to the faculty transcript scores a submission on the track's 5 x 20-point rubric via formula_executor, emits one verdict line per criterion, stores provenance (kernel block, kernel version, rubric version, run id), and routes submissions below 70 to a rewrite path.
Maintain a live weighted gradebook (memos 60, defenses 20, capstone 20) and produce a transcript PDF containing every grade id and score.

Schedule the term defense on the term's last day with pass/fail and a re-sit within 7 days on failure; accept capstone upload with two reviewer invites sent by email, collect three verdicts under the acceptance rule (all accept -> accepted, accept/accept/revise -> revise), and gate graduation on ave

Upload and edit track YAML, validate it against the schema, show a week-level diff against the current version, and pin a track version per enrolment so existing learners stay on their pinned version.
Expose per-week readings and cases with their public sources, withholding each case's outcome until the case_class session opens it for that learner.
